intro: Week 6 opens in London with Texans and Jaguars and runs through Monday night, with Minnesota, Miami, Detroit and Cincinnati on bye. Philadelphia plays without Jalen Hurts, and Chicago waits on Caleb Williams. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Jalen Hurts out with a blood clot in his calf, Tanner McKee starts
top.dek: Hurts has a superficial clot in his calf from a cleat hit against the Rams on Oct. 4. A second ultrasound Wednesday showed movement in the clot, and the Eagles ruled him out Thursday. There is no timetable for his return.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Caleb Williams is questionable for Atlanta after three missed games
top.dek: Williams has been out with a hamstring strain since Week 2 and was a full participant in practice three days running. He says he has one more test to pass. The Bears are coming off a 31-7 loss at Green Bay.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs piles up 207 scrimmage yards and passes Barry Sanders
top.dek: Gibbs ran 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the 45-21 win at Arizona, and caught five passes for 56 more. The two scores gave him 58 career touchdowns, the most by any player under 25 in league history.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 168: Denver wins with its fewest yards since John Elway's first start
top.dek: The Broncos beat Seattle 17-14 in overtime Thursday night on 168 total yards. NFL.com reports it is the first time since 1983 that Denver won with fewer than 175. Bo Nix threw for 107 yards and no touchdowns.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Texans and Jaguars open Week 6 at Wembley, 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network
top.dek: Houston is 1-4 and Jacksonville is 4-1. The Texans plan to move Will Anderson Jr., who has 7.5 sacks, around the front against a Jaguars line that starts Walker Little at left tackle.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills hit Vegas with five on the report

stories.text: Bills carry a league-best scoring offense into Las Vegas
stories.summary: Buffalo is 4-1 after a 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday night. The Bills average 32.8 points a game, tied with Detroit for the league lead, and they visit the Raiders today. Las Vegas has built its week around slowing Josh Allen.

stories.text: Five Bills are questionable, led by WR DJ Moore and DL Ed Oliver
stories.summary: Moore (shoulder) and Oliver (knee) sat out Wednesday and Thursday and went limited Friday. Joshua Palmer (shoulder) and Dee Alford (ankle) were limited all week, and T.J. Sanders (shoulder) was full on Friday. Moore, Oliver, Palmer and Alford were all inactive for the Rams game. Coach Joe Brady said anyone who is ready will play.

stories.text: Josh Allen runs for 121 yards in the Rams win
stories.summary: Allen threw for 210 yards and ran for 121 in Week 5, and he accounted for two touchdowns. Through five games he has 1,249 passing yards, 7 passing touchdowns and 8 rushing touchdowns, second most in the league.

stories.text: 13: rushing touchdowns for Buffalo, tops in the NFL
stories.summary: The Bills lead the league with 13 rushing scores through five games. Their 1,981 total yards rank second. Allen's eight rushing touchdowns account for most of the ground damage.

stories.text: At Raiders today, 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo plays at Allegiant Stadium this afternoon. The Bills then have their Week 7 bye and return Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS against the Ravens. Watch the Raiders' edge pressure from Maxx Crosby against a line that expects Spencer Brown back.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Winless Dolphins use the bye to regroup

stories.text: Winless Dolphins take the bye to fix execution
stories.summary: Miami fell to 0-5 with a 31-24 loss to the Bengals at home. The Dolphins cut an 18-point fourth-quarter deficit to seven, then missed the extra point and failed to recover an onside kick. Coach Jeff Hafley says the bye is for getting healthy and cleaning up mistakes.

stories.text: Dolphins head into the bye with a long list of bumps
stories.summary: RB Jaylen Wright (foot), edge Robert Beal Jr. (hamstring), CB Reese Taylor (quad) and WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) sat out Tuesday's practice. CB JuJu Brents left the Bengals game with a stinger, and TE Justin Joly is in the concussion protocol. RB De'Von Achane is on injured reserve and is not expected back for the Jets game.

stories.text: Rookie LB Jacob Rodriguez leads the NFL in tackles
stories.summary: Rodriguez has 57 tackles through five games, the most in the league. Fellow rookies Chris Johnson and Michael Taaffe also forced fumbles against Cincinnati. Miami has played 14 rookies, who have combined for a league-high 2,192 snaps.

stories.text: 137: passing yards for Malik Willis against the Bengals
stories.summary: Willis completed 15 of 27 passes with one touchdown and two interceptions. He also ran eight times for 74 yards and a score. Hafley said the passing game needs more consistency before the offense can climb.

stories.text: Bye this week, then at the Jets on Oct. 25
stories.summary: Miami is off in Week 6. The Dolphins play the Jets in Week 7 on Oct. 25. Watch whether cornerback Storm Duck and defensive tackle Kenneth Grant, both working back from injuries, return after the break.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots host Jets, A.J. Brown in the mix

stories.text: A.J. Brown nears a return as Patriots host the Jets
stories.summary: Brown has missed four games with a high-ankle sprain suffered in the opener against Seattle. He opened his practice window Wednesday and finished the week limited and questionable. New England enters at 3-2 after a 45-17 win over the Raiders.

stories.text: Cornerbacks Davis and Prunty out; Brown, Campbell, Henderson questionable
stories.summary: Carlton Davis III (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring) are out. Wide receiver A.J. Brown, left tackle Will Campbell (knee) and running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) are questionable after limited practice. Christian Gonzalez came off the report and expects to play. Rookie Caleb Lomu starts if Campbell cannot go.

stories.text: Drake Maye posts a season-best game against Las Vegas
stories.summary: Maye's single-game EPA against the Raiders, +28.7, is the best by any quarterback this season. Through five games he ranks fourth in success rate at 52.2% and second in completion rate over expected. He is a full participant after a shoulder issue.

stories.text: 52.4%: the Jets' blitz rate, second in the NFL
stories.summary: New York sends extra rushers more than half the time. Against Cleveland it blitzed on 63.6% of Deshaun Watson's drop-backs and sacked him eight times. Maye ranks third in EPA per play against man blitzes since the start of 2025.

stories.text: Jets at Gillette today, 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: New England hosts New York this afternoon at 1 p.m. ET. The Patriots own the 30th-ranked run defense, so watch how they handle Braelon Allen. Left tackle depth matters against a Jets front that blitzes constantly.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets try to stack wins at Gillette

stories.text: Jets snap a three-game skid, now face the Patriots
stories.summary: New York beat Cleveland 17-12 at MetLife to end a three-game losing streak, with Braelon Allen scoring late. The Jets are 2-3 and travel to New England today. Aaron Glenn is in his second season as head coach.

stories.text: Breece Hall, Adonai Mitchell and Joseph Ossai out vs. Patriots
stories.summary: Running back Breece Hall (quad), receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger), edge Joseph Ossai (ankle) and guard Dylan Parham (knee) are out. Safety Dane Belton (knee), receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) and tight end Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) are questionable.

stories.text: Rookie David Bailey leads all rookies in pressures
stories.summary: Bailey has five sacks and 20 pressures through five games, the most among rookies. He had three sacks against Cleveland. The Patriots' right tackle will see him on the offense's right side on most snaps.

stories.text: 147: Geno Smith's pass attempts without an interception
stories.summary: That stretch is third longest in the NFL. Smith completes 69.4% of his throws with six touchdowns. He has also fumbled four times, and left tackle Olu Fashanu has allowed five sacks.

stories.text: At Patriots today, 1 p.m. ET, then Dolphins Oct. 25
stories.summary: The Jets play at Gillette Stadium at 1 p.m. ET this afternoon. Next week they host Miami on Oct. 25. Watch whether Smith's short passing game, the most dink-heavy in the league, can handle New England's pass rush.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Huntley starts again at Cleveland

stories.text: Ravens go to Cleveland with Huntley under center again
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson has not practiced since hurting his ankle in the Oct. 4 game against Tennessee, so Tyler Huntley makes his second straight start. Baltimore is 4-1 and brings a three-game win streak into its first division game of the year. Trey Hendrickson looks set to return to the pass rush after missing two games.

stories.text: Jackson, Jurgens and two more Ravens ruled out
stories.summary: Jackson (ankle), center Cam Jurgens (concussion), tight end Matthew Hibner (hand) and defensive tackle Broderick Washington (ankle) are out. Wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) and guards Emery Jones Jr. (ankle) and Andrew Vorhees (foot) are questionable. Designations were set Friday and can change before kickoff.

stories.text: Huntley has not thrown an interception this season
stories.summary: Through Week 5, Huntley has completed 32 of 41 passes for 264 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, good for a 109.8 passer rating. His overtime rushing touchdown won the game in Atlanta. Baltimore needs the same clean football against a Cleveland defense that leans on man coverage.

stories.text: 3: straight one-possession wins for Baltimore
stories.summary: The Ravens have won three games in a row, all by one possession, the latest a 30-23 overtime win over Atlanta. Their margin for error is thin at quarterback, and Cleveland's offense has turned the ball over five times in its last three games. The Ravens defense has struggled on third down.

stories.text: At Browns, today at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Baltimore plays at Cleveland this afternoon. Watch whether Hendrickson and the front can get to Deshaun Watson, who has taken 19 sacks, and whether the patched offensive line holds without Jurgens. The Bengals visit Baltimore on Oct. 25.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals use the bye to heal up

stories.text: Bengals take the bye at 3-2 with penalties to clean up
stories.summary: Cincinnati beat Miami 31-24 on Oct. 11 after leading 28-10 in the fourth quarter. Zac Taylor pointed to penalties and missed chances with good field position, and called the fixes easy. The Bengals are off this week and open their divisional stretch in Baltimore on Oct. 25.

stories.text: Bozeman to IR, Hudson and Dugger being checked
stories.summary: Linebacker Swayze Bozeman broke his forearm and goes on injured reserve, though Taylor does not think the season is over for him. Tight end Tanner Hudson has a pectoral injury the team is still evaluating, and safety Kyle Dugger has a quad issue and is week to week. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins came through the Miami game without a setback.

stories.text: Burrow throws four touchdowns and no picks in Miami
stories.summary: Joe Burrow went 23 of 32 for 190 yards and four touchdowns, finding Gesicki, Perine, Hudson and Chase. Miami never sacked him. Chase caught six passes for 77 yards, including a 45-yard score over the middle.

stories.text: 22: straight field goals for Evan McPherson
stories.summary: McPherson's 26-yarder in Miami was his 22nd consecutive make, a Bengals record. The kick pushed the lead to 31-18. Taylor singled out the streak when he reviewed the game.

stories.text: Bye this week, then at Ravens Oct. 25 on CBS
stories.summary: Cincinnati is off today. The next game is a division matchup at Baltimore on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, regional coverage. Watch how healthy the Bengals are after the break and whether the Ravens have Lamar Jackson back.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns need offense against Baltimore

stories.text: Browns offense looks for answers against Baltimore
stories.summary: Cleveland ranks 27th in scoring and 29th in yards, and lost 17-12 to the Jets last week to end a three-game win streak. Deshaun Watson starts with Dillon Gabriel out, and Todd Monken faces his former team for the first time. A win would pull the Browns level with the Ravens at the top of the division.

stories.text: Gabriel and four others out for Cleveland
stories.summary: Quarterback Dillon Gabriel (back), running back Dylan Sampson (knee), guard Teven Jenkins (back) and defensive tackles Kalia Davis (quad) and Mike Hall (ankle) are out. Running back Quinshon Judkins, end Derek Barnett, defensive tackle Mason Graham and linebacker Carson Schwesinger are all questionable with ankle or knee issues. Receiver KC Concepcion cleared concussion protocol.

stories.text: Watson has 1,010 yards and 167 on the ground
stories.summary: In five games, Watson has completed 95 of 148 passes for 1,010 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions, with a 94.1 passer rating. He has also run for 167 yards. His scrambling will be a test for a Baltimore front that gets Trey Hendrickson back.

stories.text: 19: sacks taken by Watson through five games
stories.summary: Eight of them came in the loss to the Jets. The Browns have used four different starting offensive line lineups in five games. Baltimore will look to pressure him from the first series.

stories.text: Ravens at Cleveland today, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Browns host Baltimore this afternoon at Huntington Bank Field. Watch Judkins' ankle, which affects a running game averaging 3.0 yards per carry, and whether Cleveland's man coverage rattles Tyler Huntley.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Thin receiver room travels to Tampa

stories.text: Steelers face Tampa Bay with few healthy receivers
stories.summary: Michael Pittman Jr. is on injured reserve, and Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek are out for the trip to Tampa. That leaves DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Kaden Wetjen as the healthy receivers on the 53-man roster. Pittsburgh is 3-2 after a 34-22 win over Indianapolis.

stories.text: Dowdle, Freiermuth, Ramsey and Dean questionable
stories.summary: Running back Rico Dowdle (toe), tight end Pat Freiermuth (calf), cornerbacks Jalen Ramsey (wrist) and Jamel Dean (ankle), and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton (ankle) carry questionable tags. Wilson, Skowronek and safety DeShon Elliott are out. Metcalf was added late as questionable with an illness.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren piles up 188 yards against Indianapolis
stories.summary: Warren ran for 101 yards and caught six passes for 87, including an 80-yard touchdown in the first quarter. He added a 50-yard rushing score in the third. Pat Freiermuth also caught two touchdowns, and Aaron Rodgers finished 22 of 31 for 235 yards.

stories.text: 9: Rodgers' touchdown passes of 80 yards or more
stories.summary: The 80-yarder to Warren was his ninth, which ties Ben Roethlisberger for the most in NFL history. Rodgers took a hard hit from Grover Stewart on the throw. He threw three touchdowns in the game.

stories.text: At Buccaneers, today at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh visits a 1-4 Tampa Bay team that ranks second in the league against the run. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels starts for the injured Baker Mayfield, and the Steelers want to hold down Bucky Irving and make Daniels throw.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans end skid, fly to London

stories.text: Texans snap 0-4 start, now cross the Atlantic
stories.summary: Houston beat Tennessee 26-3 on Oct. 11 for its first win of the year and sits at 1-4. C.J. Stroud ran for a score and threw for another, and Will Anderson Jr. had three of the team's four sacks. The Texans now play Jacksonville in London this morning.

stories.text: Montgomery, Dell and Pitre are out in London
stories.summary: Running back David Montgomery (groin) did not make the trip, and receiver Tank Dell is still not ready to return. Safety Jalen Pitre (shoulder) is out, with rookie Kamari Ramsey set to cover his nickel snaps. Linebacker Henry To'oTo'o and defensive back Ja'Marcus Ingram are questionable.

stories.text: Stroud throws for 261 and runs one in at Tennessee
stories.summary: Stroud threw for 261 yards in the win over the Titans. He hit Jaylin Noel for a 9-yard touchdown and scored himself on a 2-yard keeper. Houston outgained Tennessee 225 to 49 yards across the second and third quarters.

stories.text: 7.5: Anderson's sacks lead the NFL through five games
stories.summary: Will Anderson Jr. has 7.5 sacks, the most in the league. Danielle Hunter has three sacks and six quarterback hits. Jacksonville left tackle Walker Little, now starting for the injured Anton Harrison, has to handle both of them today.

stories.text: At Jaguars today, 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network
stories.summary: Houston plays at Wembley Stadium in London, its first trip there since 2019 and also against Jacksonville. Coach DeMeco Ryans wants to line up four ends at once and move Anderson around. The Texans return home Oct. 25 to host the Giants.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts need a win over winless Titans

stories.text: Colts fall to 2-3 and need a win over winless Tennessee
stories.summary: Pittsburgh beat Indianapolis 34-22 last Sunday after two long touchdowns by Jaylen Warren. The Colts scored a touchdown on only one of their trips inside the Steelers' 25. They host the 0-5 Titans today.

stories.text: Tight end Tyler Warren questionable with a groin injury
stories.summary: Warren picked up the groin problem in Friday's practice and is listed questionable. He leads the Colts in targets, catches and receiving touchdowns. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) and receiver Ashton Dulin (hamstring) are out.

stories.text: Tyler Warren runs and catches in the loss to Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Warren scored on a 1-yard fourth-and-goal run in the first quarter against the Steelers. He also caught a 29-yard pass from Daniel Jones that moved the Colts inside the 5 in the third quarter. He leads Indianapolis in targets, catches and receiving touchdowns.

stories.text: 80 and 50: Jaylen Warren's touchdown yards on Sunday
stories.summary: Steelers back Jaylen Warren scored on an 80-yard catch and a 50-yard run against the Colts. Colts.com says he is the first player to do both in a game since Herschel Walker in 1986. Indianapolis gave up both plays in a 34-22 loss.

stories.text: Home against Tennessee today, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Colts host the 0-5 Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium. A win would get Indianapolis back to .500. Tennessee has scored the fewest points in the league through five games.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Little's 57-yarder lifts Jags to 4-1

stories.text: Cam Little's 57-yarder lifts Jaguars to 4-1
stories.summary: Little kicked the 57-yard field goal as time expired to beat Philadelphia 19-17 in London. Jake Elliott had put the Eagles up 17-16 with eight seconds left, and Ameer Abdullah's 53-yard kickoff return left one second on the clock. It was Jacksonville's third straight win.

stories.text: Left tackle Anton Harrison goes on injured reserve
stories.summary: Harrison hurt his right knee on a noncontact play against the Eagles and will need arthroscopic surgery after the team returns from London. He must miss at least four games, and the team could lose him for the year if the surgery finds serious damage. Walker Little takes over at left tackle, and long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) is out.

stories.text: Parker Washington scores twice against Philadelphia
stories.summary: Washington caught six passes for 124 yards and two touchdowns in the win. He took a 51-yard score early and a 27-yard fourth-and-5 touchdown that put Jacksonville ahead 16-14 late.

stories.text: 331: Trevor Lawrence's passing yards in London
stories.summary: Lawrence completed 24 of 39 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against the Eagles. The Jaguars managed just one sack and no takeaways, their first game of the year without a turnover.

stories.text: Back at Wembley today against Houston, 9:30 a.m. ET
stories.summary: Jacksonville faces the 1-4 Texans on NFL Network. Walker Little starts at left tackle against Will Anderson Jr. (7.5 sacks) and Danielle Hunter. Cornerback Montaric Brown is out and Jaylon Jones is questionable.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Saleh backs Ward after 0-5 start

stories.text: Saleh sticks with Cam Ward after 0-5 start
stories.summary: Tennessee lost 26-3 at home to Houston. Coach Robert Saleh said Ward remains the starter. The Titans have scored 58 points through five games.

stories.text: Spears questionable, Winston and Elliott out
stories.summary: Running back Tyjae Spears (knee) is listed questionable at Indianapolis. Safety Kevin Winston Jr. (quad) and defensive lineman Jordan Elliott (personal) are out.

stories.text: Cam Ward's line through five games
stories.summary: Ward has completed 63.2 percent of his passes for 896 yards, with three touchdowns and three interceptions. Against Houston he went 23 of 36 for 170 yards and one interception. The offense managed 187 total yards.

stories.text: 58: points Tennessee has scored in five games
stories.summary: That is the lowest total in the league. Tennessee has been held to 10 points or fewer three times, and the only score against Houston was a 30-yard field goal.

stories.text: At Colts today, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Titans visit Lucas Oil Stadium for a game with the 2-3 Colts. Tennessee ranks 31st in yards per play. It has lost 11 straight AFC South games.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos survive Seattle in overtime, 17-14

stories.text: Broncos edge Seahawks 17-14 in overtime on Thursday night
stories.summary: Denver improved to 4-2 when Ja'Quan McMillian intercepted Sam Darnold in overtime and Wil Lutz drilled a 53-yard field goal. Seattle had erased a 14-3 deficit with 11 straight fourth-quarter points to force the extra period. The Broncos did it with five sacks and three takeaways while playing without two starters in the secondary.

stories.text: Surtain and Hufanga both sit as Denver's secondary thins out
stories.summary: Cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle, hurt in Week 4) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle, hurt against the Chargers) were both ruled out for the Seattle game. Hufanga is expected to miss a few more games, and the team hopes Surtain returns for Week 7 at Arizona. Cornerback Riley Moss, who missed Week 5 with ribs, was questionable after three limited practices.

stories.text: McMillian's overtime pick sets up the winning kick
stories.summary: Cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian jumped a third-and-7 throw from Darnold in overtime and gave Denver the ball in field goal range. Linebacker Alex Singleton led the defense with 13 tackles. The unit held Seattle to 91 first-half yards without Surtain and Hufanga.

stories.text: 168: Denver wins with its fewest yards since 1983
stories.summary: The Broncos gained 168 total yards against Seattle. NFL.com reports it is the first time since John Elway's first start in 1983 that Denver won a game with fewer than 175 yards. Bo Nix finished 17 of 27 for 107 yards with two sacks and no touchdown passes.

stories.text: Broncos head to Arizona on Oct. 25
stories.summary: Denver is listed at the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS at State Farm Stadium. Watch how much the offense improves after a 168-yard night, and whether Surtain is back. Sean Payton took over play calling the week before the Seattle game.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Unbeaten Chiefs host winless Chargers without Rice

stories.text: Unbeaten Chiefs host winless Chargers short on receivers
stories.summary: Kansas City is 4-0 and plays Los Angeles (0-5) at Arrowhead today at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. Andy Reid ruled out receiver Rashee Rice on Friday, so Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy and a group of young receivers carry the passing game. Reid is 22-5 coming off a bye, though he has lost two of his last three post-bye games.

stories.text: Rice and Simmons ruled out against the Chargers
stories.summary: Rice has a hamstring injury he suffered in the first quarter of the Week 4 win over the Raiders and did not practice all week. Left tackle Josh Simmons also is out after returning to practice Wednesday for the first time in nearly two months. Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed is questionable.

stories.text: Mahomes is playing his best ball since 2022
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes has thrown nine touchdowns against two interceptions, and Yahoo Sports calls this his best start since 2022. With Rice out, he will lean on Kelce and Worthy against a Chargers pass defense allowing fewer than 200 passing yards per game.

stories.text: 537: Kenneth Walker III's rushing yards through four games
stories.summary: Walker has 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns, averaging 6.2 yards per carry and 134 yards per game. The Chargers allow 118.6 rushing yards per game, so the Chiefs have a clear path to lean on him.

stories.text: Chargers today, then two road trips
stories.summary: Kansas City hosts Los Angeles today at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch how the Chiefs defense, which is allowing 317.8 yards per game, handles a banged-up Chargers offense. The next two games are at Seattle and at Denver.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders try to snap two-game skid against Bills

stories.text: Raiders look to end a two-game slide against Buffalo
stories.summary: Las Vegas started 3-0 and has lost two straight. The Raiders host the 4-1 Bills at Allegiant Stadium today. Buffalo averages 32.8 points per game, tied for the league lead, so the Raiders defense has a big job.

stories.text: Three Raiders ruled out, guard Zuhn questionable
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (concussion), tight end Carter Runyon (foot) and receiver Dont'e Thornton Jr. (hamstring) are out. Guard Trey Zuhn III (knee) is questionable. Buffalo listed five players as questionable, including Ed Oliver and DJ Moore.

stories.text: Bowers is back and producing over 100 yards a game
stories.summary: Brock Bowers missed Weeks 1 and 2 with an injury and has scored a touchdown in all three games since. He is averaging better than 100 receiving yards per game and sits second among tight ends, four yards behind Sam LaPorta.

stories.text: 10: Raiders takeaways, tied for most in the NFL
stories.summary: The Las Vegas defense has forced 10 turnovers. Maxx Crosby has 36 pressures, tied for third in the league, with 20 coming in the two home games. Buffalo has committed nine giveaways over its last three games.

stories.text: Bills at Allegiant Stadium, 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Raiders kick off at 1:25 p.m. PT today, which is 4:25 p.m. ET, on CBS with Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt. The main task is containing Josh Allen, who leads quarterbacks with 239 rushing yards. Buffalo played Monday night, so it comes in on a short week.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers travel to unbeaten Kansas City

stories.text: Harbaugh owns a costly fourth-down call after 0-5 start
stories.summary: The Chargers lost 23-17 to Denver after Jim Harbaugh went for it on fourth-and-1 in the fourth quarter. He apologized for the call, and Denver scored five plays later. Los Angeles is 0-5 for the first time since 2003 and has lost eight straight dating to last season.

stories.text: Alt, James and Harris out at Kansas City
stories.summary: The Friday report lists tackle Joe Alt, guard Kayode Awosika, receiver Tre' Harris, cornerback Donte Jackson and safety Derwin James Jr. as out. Receivers Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Marquez Valdes-Scantling carried no game status. Four rookies started on the offensive line last week.

stories.text: Herbert takes five sacks and keeps pushing
stories.summary: Justin Herbert went 14 of 24 for 121 yards with one touchdown and one interception against Denver. He was sacked five times and lost a fourth-quarter fumble, giving him nine turnovers in five games. Harbaugh said he will not ask Herbert to play differently.

stories.text: 8: straight losses, the longest of Harbaugh's career
stories.summary: The Chargers have lost eight in a row dating to last season, according to ESPN Research, the longest streak of Harbaugh's head-coaching career. Herbert has seven interceptions, tied for the league lead.

stories.text: At Kansas City today, 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Los Angeles visits the 4-0 Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. Watch the receiver room, where several starters entered the week hurt, and whether the line can protect Herbert after five sacks last week. A loss would make the Chargers 0-6.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys try to fix defense at Lambeau

stories.text: Cowboys lose to winless Tampa Bay, fall to 2-3
stories.summary: Dallas was a 9.5-point favorite on Oct. 8 and lost 24-16 to a Buccaneers team that had not won yet. Tampa Bay outscored the Cowboys 17-0 in the third quarter and ran for 241 yards. Dallas has since moved Christian Parker to the coaching booth and added Mike Pettine as a senior defensive advisor.

stories.text: Cowboys without Shelton and Durant at Green Bay
stories.summary: Tackle Drew Shelton and cornerback Cobie Durant are out with hamstring injuries after missing every practice this week. Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, defensive tackle L.T. Overton, and cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. and Ameer Speed are all questionable. CeeDee Lamb (thigh) practiced fully and is not listed with a game status.

stories.text: Dak Prescott booed in loss to Tampa Bay
stories.summary: Prescott finished 24 of 42 for 316 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions against the Buccaneers. He was 13 of 27 for 117 yards through the third quarter before a late push, and fans booed after a fourth-down throw fell incomplete. Tampa Bay corners held Lamb to 9 yards on five targets through three quarters.

stories.text: 241: rushing yards Dallas allowed to Tampa Bay
stories.summary: The Buccaneers piled up 241 yards on the ground, including a 72-yard run by Bucky Irving. Dallas now gives up 168.8 rushing yards per game this season. The Cowboys have five sacks through five games.

stories.text: Cowboys visit Packers on Sunday night
stories.summary: Dallas (2-3) plays at Green Bay (3-2) at Lambeau Field on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Watch a secondary missing Durant, and whether Porter plays. Micah Parsons remains on injured reserve and will not play.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Winston leads Giants into first place

stories.text: Winston keeps Giants atop the NFC East
stories.summary: Jameis Winston threw for 326 yards and three touchdowns on Oct. 11 as the Giants rallied from a 27-13 deficit to tie Washington 27-27 in overtime. New York is 3-1-1 and leads the division. The Giants also acquired QB JJ McCarthy from Minnesota for a fifth-round pick, and he made his debut in that game.

stories.text: Giants wait on Thomas, Eluemunor and Carter
stories.summary: Left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin), right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf) are questionable after limited work Friday. Tight end Theo Johnson, safety Tyler Nubin and cornerback Colton Hood are out. If Thomas cannot go, rookie J.C. Davis starts at left tackle.

stories.text: Likely and Nabers each top 100 yards in the tie
stories.summary: Isaiah Likely caught 11 passes for 94 yards and two touchdowns against Washington, and his second score held up on replay. Malik Nabers also had 11 catches for 121 yards, including the 17-yard tying touchdown with 1:43 left.

stories.text: 2 of 5: Zvada's field goals in the Washington tie
stories.summary: Giants kicker Dominic Zvada made two of five field goal tries on Oct. 11, with misses from 50, 57 and 46 yards in the rain. Seven of his 14 attempts this season have come from 50 yards or longer. Coach John Harbaugh has said he still trusts him.

stories.text: Giants host Saints at MetLife on Sunday
stories.summary: New York (3-1-1) hosts New Orleans (1-4) on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Saints rank 30th against the run and allow 30.2 points per game. Watch whether the Giants lean on the ground game, which averages about 3.5 yards per carry.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles turn to McKee as Hurts sits

stories.text: Hurts out with calf blood clot, McKee starts
stories.summary: Jalen Hurts has a superficial blood clot in his calf from a cleat hit against the Rams on Oct. 4. A second ultrasound Wednesday showed movement in the clot, and the Eagles ruled him out Thursday. There is no timetable for his return, and Tanner McKee starts against Carolina.

stories.text: Barkley out, DeVonta Smith set to return
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is out after not practicing all week, and Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) is out too. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) returns after a full Friday practice. Center Drew Kendall (knee) is questionable.

stories.text: Tanner McKee gets his third career start
stories.summary: McKee, a sixth-round pick in 2023, starts for the first time outside Week 18. He took the first-team reps this week and worked on the game plan with offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. Smith's return and Dameon Pierce's carries should shape the offense around him.

stories.text: 301.3: Carolina's passing yards per game, second in the NFL
stories.summary: The Panthers throw for 301.3 yards a game behind Bryce Young and receiver Tetairoa McMillan, who had 14 catches for 192 yards against Detroit. Carolina also allows 156.5 rushing yards per game. Philadelphia's red zone touchdown rate is 50 percent.

stories.text: Eagles host Panthers at the Linc on Sunday
stories.summary: Philadelphia (2-3) faces Carolina (2-2, off a bye) on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Eagles lost close games to the Rams and Jaguars and need to finish a full 60 minutes. Their cornerbacks face a deep Carolina receiver group.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders face 5-0 49ers on Monday

stories.text: Commanders botch final play of tie with Giants
stories.summary: With 12 seconds left in overtime and no timeouts, Jayden Daniels held the ball on a pass play and was tackled for no gain as the clock expired. The game ended 27-27. Coach Dan Quinn said the sequencing of the play was on him, not Daniels.

stories.text: Croskey-Merritt out, Diggs questionable for MNF
stories.summary: Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is out, Quinn confirmed Saturday. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler should absorb his snaps, with Jeremy McNichols also available. Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is questionable after limited practices, and quarterback Marcus Mariota is out with a knee injury.

stories.text: Daniels runs for 103 in return from elbow injury
stories.summary: Daniels came back from a dislocated left elbow against the Giants and went 17 of 25 for 199 yards. He also ran for 103 yards and two touchdowns. He practiced fully Thursday and Friday and is expected to start Monday.

stories.text: 103: Daniels' rushing yards in the tie with New York
stories.summary: Daniels carried Washington on the ground with 103 yards and two scores, in his first game after a second elbow dislocation. He wore a brace on his left elbow. Washington led 12-3 at halftime and finished with a tie.

stories.text: Commanders visit unbeaten 49ers Monday night
stories.summary: Washington (1-3-1) plays at San Francisco (5-0) on Monday, Oct. 19, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN. Daniels is on track to start while Diggs is a game-time call. Washington has its bye right after this game.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Williams nears return in Atlanta

stories.text: Caleb Williams closes in on his return after three missed games
stories.summary: Williams has sat out three games with a hamstring strain he picked up in Week 2 against Minnesota. He was a full participant in practice three days running and is listed as questionable for Atlanta. He says he has one more test to pass before he plays, and the team expects clarity before it flies out Saturday. Chicago needs him after a 31-7 loss at Green Bay.

stories.text: Four Bears ruled out, three more questionable at Atlanta
stories.summary: Running back Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe), linebackers T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Keyshaun Elliott (quad), and lineman Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) are out. Quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) and defensive backs Kyler Gordon (calf) and Tyrique Stevenson (hip) are questionable. Gordon is also on injured reserve, so the team must clear a roster spot to activate him.

stories.text: Austin Booker leads Chicago with four sacks
stories.summary: The defensive end has 4.0 sacks this season, tops on the roster. He has 7.5 over his last nine games, counting last year. With Montez Sweat serving a two-game suspension and Odeyingbo out, Booker carries more of the pass rush in Atlanta.

stories.text: 42.9%: Chicago's red zone touchdown rate, lowest in the NFL
stories.summary: The Bears have reached the 20 on 21 drives, tied for second most in the league. They score touchdowns on fewer than half of those trips. Chicago also leads the league in rushing at 173.2 yards per game, so the fix has to come from finishing drives.

stories.text: Bears visit Falcons today at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Chicago (3-2) plays at Atlanta (2-3), and the matchup pairs the NFL's two best rushing offenses. Bijan Robinson leads the league with 580 rushing yards. Watch Williams' first snaps back and whether the Bears protect the ball after a five-turnover game in Green Bay.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions rest after a 45-21 rout

stories.text: Lions hit the bye on a high after beating Arizona 45-21
stories.summary: Detroit is off this week at 3-2. The offense rolled in Week 5 and the pass rush piled up five sacks. The back end is the open question: the Lions switched to man coverage on 31 percent of snaps against Arizona, up from about 16 percent in the first four games.

stories.text: Branch and Mays are the Lions' hopes to return after the bye
stories.summary: Safety Brian Branch is coming back from an Achilles tear he suffered late last season. Center Cade Mays has been out since fracturing his wrist in training camp. Coach Dan Campbell hopes both are available after the break, when Green Bay visits Ford Field.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs piles up 207 scrimmage yards in Arizona
stories.summary: Gibbs ran 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns and caught five passes for 56 more. The two scores gave him 58 career touchdowns, more than any player under 25 in league history, passing Barry Sanders.

stories.text: 28: Jared Goff's active streak of games with a touchdown pass
stories.summary: Goff threw three touchdowns against Arizona, going 19 of 30 for 271 yards with no interceptions. The 28-game run is the longest active streak in the NFL and a franchise record. He has gone five straight games without an interception.

stories.text: Lions are on bye, then host Green Bay on Oct. 25
stories.summary: Detroit has no game today. The next one is Sunday, Oct. 25, at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX against the Packers at Ford Field. Minnesota visits Ford Field the week after. Watch whether the pass defense improves and who returns from injury.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers host Cowboys on Sunday night

stories.text: Packers ride five takeaways into Sunday night against Dallas
stories.summary: Green Bay beat Chicago 31-7 last week, forcing three interceptions and two fumbles. That was the team's biggest takeaway day since 2016. Safety Xavier McKinney had two of the picks. The Packers now host the Cowboys tonight at Lambeau Field.

stories.text: Four Packers out and five questionable for Dallas
stories.summary: Receiver Skyy Moore, cornerback Benjamin St-Juste, and defensive tackles Jonathan Ford and Javon Hargrave are out. Hargrave tore an Achilles and is done for the year. Cornerback Brandon Cisse, guard Aaron Banks, lineman Jacob Monk, tackle Anthony Campbell and receiver Savion Williams are questionable. Coach Matt LaFleur confirmed cornerback Keisean Nixon will play.

stories.text: Jordan Love torches Chicago for 367 yards
stories.summary: Love had only six incompletions and finished with a 137.5 passer rating. He hit Christian Watson on touchdown throws of 42 and 53 yards. Chicago allowed five completions of 30-plus air yards to Love, tying an ESPN-tracked record for one game.

stories.text: 60.4: Green Bay's rushing yards per game, last in the NFL
stories.summary: The Packers throw for 271.0 yards a game, fourth best in the league, and run for the fewest. That lopsided approach worked against Chicago. The question is whether it holds up as the weather turns cold at Lambeau.

stories.text: Cowboys at Lambeau tonight, 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: Green Bay (3-2) hosts Dallas (2-3) on Sunday Night Football. Dak Prescott has 1,381 passing yards and nine touchdowns, and CeeDee Lamb has 507 receiving yards. Watch whether the Packers keep taking the ball away and how their thinned defensive line holds up.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings take the bye

stories.text: Unbeaten Vikings carry a 10-game win streak into the bye
stories.summary: Minnesota is 5-0 after beating New Orleans 23-13, and the winning streak reaches back to last season. The Vikings sit idle in Week 6. The Saints managed 96 passing yards and went 2 of 10 on third down.

stories.text: Jordan Mason expected back from thumb surgery after the bye
stories.summary: The running back has been out since the season opener with a broken thumb and had surgery. Coach Kevin O'Connell expects Mason back for the Colts game in Week 7. Minnesota has leaned on Jones in his absence, with 410 rushing yards and two touchdowns so far.

stories.text: Kyler Murray goes 24 of 30 in win over Saints
stories.summary: Murray threw for 229 yards and a touchdown to Justin Jefferson, posting a 109.6 rating. He also ran 10 times for 51 yards. The Vikings have not lost since last season.

stories.text: 58: points the Vikings defense has allowed in five games
stories.summary: That is 12 fewer than Jacksonville, the next best, at 70. Minnesota ranks third in total defense at 259.8 yards per game. Coordinator Brian Flores sends extra rushers 57.2 percent of the time, well above Tampa Bay's 37.6 percent, the next highest rate.

stories.text: Vikings are on bye, then host Indianapolis on Oct. 25
stories.summary: Minnesota has no game today. The Colts come to U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Indianapolis is 2-3. Watch for Mason's return to the backfield.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Penix cleared to face Bears after rib scare

stories.text: Penix says ribs are fine as Falcons try to rebound from overtime loss
stories.summary: Atlanta blew a 23-15 lead in the final minute against Baltimore and lost 30-23 in overtime on Sunday night. Michael Penix Jr. took a hit late in regulation and sat out the extra period, but he practiced fully this week and expects to start against Chicago. The Falcons are 2-3 and host a Bears team that is 3-2.

stories.text: Henderson out, Za'Darius Smith questionable vs. Bears
stories.summary: Cornerback C.J. Henderson (groin) is out, which leaves Mike Hughes and Avieon Terrell as the likely starters on the outside. Edge rusher Za'Darius Smith is questionable with a neck injury after clearing concussion protocol. Penix (ribs) carries no designation, and receiver Drake London (hip) was limited on Friday.

stories.text: Drake London is having the best start of his career
stories.summary: London has 27 catches for 488 yards through five games, an average of 18.1 yards a catch. He leads the league with 408 receiving yards over Weeks 3 through 5, nearly 100 more than the next player, Brock Bowers. His hip kept him limited in Friday practice, so watch his snaps early.

stories.text: 40: Dexter and Dorlus lead all tackle duos in pressures
stories.summary: Gervon Dexter Sr. and Brandon Dorlus have 20 pressures each, the most combined by any defensive tackle pair in the league. The next-closest duo trails by eight. Dexter's 14.5 percent pressure rate tops all defensive tackles.

stories.text: Bears visit Atlanta today at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Chicago (3-2) comes to Mercedes-Benz Stadium for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on FOX. Caleb Williams has missed three games with a hamstring strain, and coach Ben Johnson called his status fluid, so the Falcons may see Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum. Atlanta's pass rush against that quarterback question is the matchup to watch.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Line thinned by injuries before trip to Philly

stories.text: Panthers carry a banged-up offensive line into Philadelphia
stories.summary: Left tackle Ikem Ekwonu has a ruptured patellar tendon and will miss a big chunk of the season. Right tackle Taylor Moton is dealing with blood clots in his lung and was on the non-football injury list and is questionable. Rookie Monroe Freeling and guard Damien Lewis are also nursing injuries, and the Eagles bring Jalen Carter's pass rush.

stories.text: Dillon out, Freeling doubtful for Panthers at Eagles
stories.summary: Running back AJ Dillon (ankle) is out and rookie tackle Monroe Freeling (knee) is doubtful. tackle Taylor Moton (lung), guard Damien Lewis (elbow), defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton (neck), running back Trevor Etienne (ankle) and edge rusher Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) are all questionable.

stories.text: Tetairoa McMillan is producing at a top 10 clip
stories.summary: McMillan has 385 receiving yards in four games, 10th in the NFL. He caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit. He will face a big Eagles secondary with Quinyon Mitchell, Riq Woolen and Cooper DeJean.

stories.text: 156.5: Rushing yards the Panthers allow per game
stories.summary: Only one defense in the league gives up more on the ground. Carolina also ranks 29th in yards allowed and 26th in points allowed. NFL.com lists Saquon Barkley (hamstring) as out, while another preview has him questionable, so check inactives for who carries the load.

stories.text: Panthers at Eagles today, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Carolina (2-2) visits Lincoln Financial Field to face a 2-3 Philadelphia team that has lost three straight. Jalen Hurts is out with a calf blood clot, so Tanner McKee starts. Bryce Young has nine touchdowns and two interceptions this season.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Three straight home losses sink Saints to 1-4

stories.text: Saints drop third straight at home, 23-13 to Vikings
stories.summary: New Orleans fell to 1-4 with a 23-13 loss to Minnesota on Oct. 11. A kickoff-return fumble and a Tyler Shough interception set up Minnesota's go-ahead stretch in the third quarter. All three of the Saints' losses in this streak came in the Superdome.

stories.text: Kamara and Olave questionable for the Giants game
stories.summary: Running back Alvin Kamara (back) and receiver Chris Olave (illness) are both questionable. Linebackers Kaden Elliss (calf) and Anfernee Jennings (knee) are out. Defensive back Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) and defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd (illness) are also questionable.

stories.text: Jonas Sanker supplied the Saints' one big play
stories.summary: The safety scooped up a fumble and ran 87 yards for a touchdown with 2:34 left in the third quarter, tying the game at 13. Kicker Daniel Carlson then missed the extra point. It was the only big swing New Orleans got in a game where the offense managed 142 total yards.

stories.text: 96: Tyler Shough's passing yards on 25 attempts
stories.summary: Shough went 16 of 25 for 96 yards and two interceptions against Minnesota. The Saints finished with 142 total yards and took six penalties for 41 yards. The offense has to find some downfield life against the Giants.

stories.text: Saints at Giants today, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: New Orleans (1-4) travels to MetLife Stadium to face New York (3-1-1). The Giants list tackles Andrew Thomas and Jermaine Eluemunor and edge rusher Abdul Carter as questionable. The all-time series is tied at 17-17.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Rookie Daniels gets a third start as Mayfield sits

stories.text: Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels starts again with Mayfield out
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield is out for Pittsburgh with a dislocated right thumb he suffered in the Week 3 loss to Minnesota. Daniels will make his third straight start after going 19 of 25 for 189 yards and a touchdown in last week's win over Dallas. Todd Bowles said Mayfield may return in Week 7 at Carolina.

stories.text: Winfield out with ribs, Morrison doubtful vs. Steelers
stories.summary: Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) is out and was expected to miss two to four weeks. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is doubtful after missing two straight games. Running back Sean Tucker, linebackers SirVocea Dennis and Josiah Trotter, and cornerback Ayden Garnes are questionable.

stories.text: Bucky Irving ran wild against Dallas
stories.summary: Irving rushed for a career-high 165 yards and had 175 yards from scrimmage. It was his first game with both a rushing and receiving touchdown, and he broke a 72-yard run. He forced a career-high 10 missed tackles.

stories.text: 72.8: Rushing yards per game the Bucs allow, second in the NFL
stories.summary: Tampa Bay's run defense sits behind only one team in the league. The Bucs have held opponents to a 33.9 percent third-down conversion rate, tied for eighth. They allowed 33 points in the opener and 16 against Dallas last week.

stories.text: Steelers at Raymond James today, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Tampa Bay (1-4) hosts Pittsburgh (3-2), led by Aaron Rodgers, who has said this is his final season. Rodgers has thrown three touchdown passes in each of the Steelers' last three games. Watch whether the Bucs' run defense can force Pittsburgh into third downs.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Harrison traded as Cardinals reset

stories.text: Cardinals trade Marvin Harrison Jr. to Houston
stories.summary: Arizona agreed to send the receiver and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Texans for a 2027 second-round pick and a sixth. It is the loudest move yet in first-year coach Mike LaFleur's roster rebuild. The Cardinals sit at 1-4 after a 45-21 home loss to Detroit.

stories.text: Rookie back Jeremiyah Love is out against the Rams
stories.summary: Love did not practice all week with a lingering left ankle injury, and the team ruled him out. He leads Arizona with 245 rushing yards. LaFleur said there is no talk of injured reserve, and the staff will re-evaluate him daily.

stories.text: Brissett throws for 292 and three scores in a blowout loss
stories.summary: Jacoby Brissett completed 29 of 47 passes with three touchdowns and one interception against Detroit. Tight end Trey McBride caught nine passes for 66 yards and a score. The effort did not stop a fourth straight loss.

stories.text: 8: straight losses to NFC West opponents
stories.summary: Arizona has dropped eight in a row inside its division, according to TSN's report on Love. The streak now carries into SoFi Stadium, where the Cardinals face a Rams team that beat them in Week 18 last season.

stories.text: At Rams today, 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Arizona visits SoFi Stadium for a Sunday kickoff. Love, safety Wydett Williams Jr. and safety Andrew Wingard are out, and safety Budda Baker and linebacker Zaven Collins are questionable. Watch how the offense gets the ball moving without its lead back.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams chase answers after Buffalo loss

stories.text: Rams look to fix special teams after overtime loss
stories.summary: Coach Sean McVay said he will evaluate the whole special teams unit, and called the kicking group not good enough. The Rams lost 37-34 in overtime to Buffalo on Monday night and sit at 2-3.

stories.text: Rams list two defensive backs as questionable
stories.summary: Cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin) and safety Kamren Curl (ankle) carry questionable tags for the Arizona game. No Rams player is ruled out. Both would be key to slowing Jacoby Brissett's passing game.

stories.text: Puka Nacua catches 17 passes in the loss to Buffalo
stories.summary: Nacua finished with 138 yards and a touchdown on 24 targets from Matthew Stafford. Only Brandon Marshall in 2009 and Chris Chambers in 2005 have seen more targets in one game. Nacua said the team must decide what its identity is.

stories.text: 1,572: passing yards for Matthew Stafford
stories.summary: Stafford has thrown for 1,572 yards with nine touchdowns and six interceptions through five games. Arizona's Jacoby Brissett has 1,110 yards. The Rams beat the Cardinals 37-20 last January, when Stafford threw four touchdowns.

stories.text: Host Arizona today, 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Rams play at SoFi Stadium in a game they cannot afford to give away at 2-3. Arizona has lost four straight and will be without running back Jeremiyah Love. Watch the kicking game after the Rams' special teams criticism.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Unbeaten 49ers face a thin receiver room

stories.text: 49ers rally past Seattle to stay unbeaten
stories.summary: San Francisco beat the Seahawks 32-29 on Oct. 11 to move to 5-0. Brock Purdy led a fourth-quarter comeback, and Eddy Pineiro's field goal with 1:56 left gave the 49ers the lead for good.

stories.text: Bosa, Evans and Deebo Samuel all hurt before Monday night
stories.summary: Nick Bosa (calf) and Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles soreness) did not practice Thursday. Deebo Samuel's hamstring will cost him several weeks, and coach Kyle Shanahan did not rule out injured reserve. Shanahan said he was hoping Bosa could go.

stories.text: Mike Evans posts 113 yards and a touchdown in Seattle
stories.summary: Evans caught seven passes for 113 yards and a score against the Seahawks. He did it while playing through rib pain for the second straight game. His status for Monday is one to watch.

stories.text: 7: turnovers in the 49ers-Seahawks game, a season high
stories.summary: The Oct. 11 game produced seven combined turnovers, the most in an NFL game this season. Renardo Green had two interceptions for San Francisco, and Gracen Halton forced and recovered a fumble for a touchdown.

stories.text: Commanders at Levi's Stadium, Monday 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Washington arrives at 1-3-1 against the 5-0 49ers. Purdy has completed 69 percent of his passes for 1,196 yards, 13 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. Watch who catches passes with Samuel out and Evans in doubt.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks fall in OT, 3-3

stories.text: Seahawks fall to Denver in overtime
stories.summary: Denver won 17-14 on Wil Lutz's 53-yard field goal after Ja'Quan McMillian intercepted Sam Darnold in overtime. Seattle drops to 3-3 and has lost twice in five days. Coach Mike Macdonald said the team has things to fix quickly.

stories.text: Tight end Elijah Arroyo hurts his shoulder
stories.summary: Arroyo left late in the first half in Denver with an apparent right shoulder injury after diving for a fumble. The team has not given a diagnosis in the coverage reviewed. Seattle hosts Kansas City next Sunday.

stories.text: Rashid Shaheed sparks the late comeback
stories.summary: Shaheed returned a punt 31 yards to set up Seattle's tying drive and caught Darnold's two-point pass to cut Denver's lead to 14-11. Jason Myers then kicked a 34-yard field goal with three seconds left to force overtime. Shaheed also lost a fumble in the first half.

stories.text: 7: interceptions for Sam Darnold, tied for the league lead
stories.summary: Darnold threw two more against Denver, and Newsweek reports he was sacked five times. He went 27 of 51 for 278 yards without a touchdown. Macdonald said the performance was not good enough but that the coaches love him.

stories.text: Chiefs at Seattle, Sunday Oct. 25, 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: Seattle is off the field today after Thursday's game and returns home next week for Sunday Night Football. Watch whether Darnold cuts down on turnovers against Kansas City.
